He also earned a sports teaching diploma. His Nobel-winning NMR work began much later at ETH Zurich in the 1970s-1980s.

After his dissertation (1960) and MD (1961), he spent a year at Harvard before returning to Karolinska.

name: Claude Cohen-Tannoudji
milestone_by_age_26: At age 26 (April 1959), had completed ENS (1957) and agrégation, finished military service, and was just beginning doctoral research under Kastler and Brossel. The 'light shift' discovery and thesis defense came in 1962 (age 29). Nobel-winning laser cooling work was in the 1980s-1990s. No material milestone by 26 found.
early_history_summary: Cohen-Tannoudji grew up in Algiers in a modest Jewish family that fled Spain during the Inquisition. He was admitted second to the École Normale Supérieure in 1953, where he studied under Henri Cartan, Laurent Schwartz, and Alfred Kastler. He joined Kastler's research group in 1955, completed the agrégation in 1957, did military service (1957-1959), then began his doctoral thesis on quantum theory of optical pumping in 1959. The thesis was defended in 1962.
family_context_summary: Born in Constantine, Algeria to a modest Sephardic Jewish family originally from Tangier. Family moved to Algiers in 1938 after anti-Semitic demonstrations. Survived Vichy discrimination during WWII.
parent_family_domain_summary: No scientific domain expertise in the family. Family was modest; no evidence of parental academic background.

name: Yoshinori Ohsumi
milestone_by_age_26: Was a graduate student at the University of Tokyo at age 26 (1971); completed B.Sci. in 1967 (age 22) and D.Sci. in 1974 (age 29). Nobel-winning autophagy discoveries were made in the 1990s. No material milestone by 26 found.

He entered the University of Tokyo to study chemistry but switched to molecular biology. He joined Kazutomo Imahori's lab as a graduate student studying protein synthesis in E. coli, with poor results. After his doctorate (1974), he did postdoctoral work at Rockefeller University before returning to the University of Tokyo. His groundbreaking autophagy work began in 1988.
family_context_summary: Father was a professor of engineering at Kyushu University. Family struggled during postwar Japan; mother had tuberculosis. Brother was 12 years older and brought science books home from Tokyo.

name: James Cronin

He completed his PhD in experimental nuclear physics under Samuel Allison in 1955, then joined Brookhaven National Laboratory. In 1958 he moved to Princeton, where the Nobel-winning CP violation experiment was conducted in 1964.
family_context_summary: Father was a professor of classical languages (PhD from University of Chicago); mother came from an upper-middle-class family (grandfather was on the Chicago Board of Trade). Family lived in academic settings.

name: George Soros
milestone_by_age_26: Had completed BSc (1951, age 21) and MSc (1954, age 24) from London School of Economics. By age 26 (1956), was moving to New York for an entry-level arbitrage position at F.M. He worked as a railway porter and nightclub waiter while studying at the London School of Economics, where he was influenced by Karl Popper's philosophy. After graduating, he worked at British merchant banks before moving to New York in 1956 to work in arbitrage. His fortune came decades later with the Quantum Fund, founded in 1969-1970.
family_context_summary: Born to a prosperous non-observant Jewish family in Budapest. Father was a lawyer and Esperanto author; mother's family operated a successful silk store. Family survived WWII by purchasing false identity documents.

name: Martinus J. G. Veltman

PhD was completed in 1963 (age 32). Nobel-winning work on electroweak renormalization with 't Hooft came in the early 1970s. No material milestone by 26 found.
early_history_summary: Veltman grew up in Waalwijk, Netherlands, the fourth of six children. His father was a primary school headmaster. He started studying at Utrecht University in 1948 but was a mediocre student initially, taking two extra years. He discovered physics through a popular book on relativity after his candidaats exam. After military service (1958-1959), he became a PhD student under Leon Van Hove, completing his doctorate in 1963. His Nobel-winning work with student Gerard 't Hooft on renormalization of Yang-Mills theory came in the early 1970s.
family_context_summary: Father was a primary school headmaster; several aunts and uncles were also primary school teachers. Family valued education but was not wealthy. Mother's father was a contractor and café owner.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a school headmaster, providing an education-valuing environment, but no physics or science domain expertise.
evidence_summary: Veltman was still a struggling university student at age 26, having taken longer than normal due to poor language aptitude and a late discovery of physics. In 1960, he received a Fulbright Scholarship to study at the University of Pennsylvania, earning his PhD in 1963 under Allan R. Day. He then did postdoctoral work with Herbert C. Brown at Purdue (1966-1972), where he began the organometallic chemistry work that led to the Nobel-winning Negishi coupling in the 1970s.
